### Issue Description

Setting `NEXT_PRIVATE_OIDC_PROMPT` to an empty string should omit the `prompt` parameter from the OIDC authorize request, as documented in `.env.example` ("an empty string will omit the prompt parameter") and the self-hosting environment docs ("Set to empty string to omit"). #2037 implemented this for #2036. #2421 rewrote the block, and since v2.6.0 an empty value falls back to `login`, so a `prompt` is now always sent (`packages/auth/server/lib/utils/handle-oauth-authorize-url.ts`, `let prompt = options.prompt ?? 'login'` followed by an unconditional `url.searchParams.set('prompt', prompt)`). The regression was reported in comments on #2421 and #2036, but no issue tracks it.

This matters for providers that want plain SSO: a signed-in user gets a code without interaction, and a signed-out user sees the login form. Each remaining value breaks a case: `none` fails for signed-out users, `login` forces re-authentication every time, and `consent` depends on how the provider handles an unasked consent.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure OIDC and set `NEXT_PRIVATE_OIDC_PROMPT=""`.
2. Click "Sign in with OIDC".
3. Inspect the redirect to the provider's authorize endpoint.

### Expected Behavior

The authorize URL has no `prompt` parameter.

### Current Behavior

The authorize URL contains `prompt=login`.

### Suggested fix

Treat an explicitly empty `NEXT_PRIVATE_OIDC_PROMPT` as "omit" and set the parameter only when a prompt remains. Keep the `select_account` default for the SSO route (`routes/oauth.ts`) when the variable is unset.

### Version

v2.18.0 (self-hosted, official Docker image)

### Issue Description

This covers the Audit Log pages appended to the sealed PDF only. I am not raising the Signing Certificate page, which labels its timestamps as UTC and is correct.

The Audit Log header lists the envelope time zone as America/Chicago. Every event timestamp below that header is rendered in UTC, with no zone label. A reader has no way to tell from the page which zone applies.

More telling is the header itself. The Created At and Last Updated fields carry an explicit (UTC) suffix, directly beside the Time Zone: America/Chicago field. The event entries carry no suffix at all.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a document with the time zone set to America/Chicago.
2. Send it to a recipient and complete signing.
3. Open the sealed PDF and compare the Audit Log pages against the Signing Certificate page.

[Pdf Signature.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32540124/Pdf.Signature.pdf)

### Expected Behavior

UTC may be a deliberate choice for the audit log, since a fixed zone is easier to display in a dispute than a per-envelope one. I do not object to UTC. The problem is not the zone; the problem is that the event entries do not name their zone while the header names a different one.

Either of these would resolve it:

1. Render event timestamps in the envelope time zone, with the zone abbreviation.
2. Keep UTC and append "UTC" to each event timestamp, matching the Created At field.

The Audit Log renders every event timestamp in UTC with no zone label. The header on the same page states the time zone as America/Chicago. A signing completed at 4:50 PM CDT appears in the Audit Log as 9:50 PM.

items.body:
This covers the document completion email only. I am not raising attachments on invite or pending emails.

Documenso attaches the sealed PDF of every envelope item to the "Signing Complete!" email, for the owner and for every notified recipient. The attachment is built in `send-document-completed-emails.handler.ts:86-99`, before any email setting is read, and passed to both `sendMail` calls at `:153` and `:253`. No setting turns it off. There is no size check anywhere in the path.

I run 2.18.0 self-hosted against Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Email Delivery, on the `smtp-auth` transport with plain username and password. OCI caps messages at 2 MB. Base64 encoding adds roughly 37 percent, so a sealed document over about 1.4 MB is already too large before headers. The provider returns a 500 and the send fails.

The fan-out at `:180` is a `Promise.all`, so one rejected send rejects the whole job and the remaining recipients are never processed, which is #3038. The handler has no `io.runTask` checkpoint, so the job replays from the first recipient across all three retries, which is #3190. A provider size cap rejects every send the same way. The document is sealed and complete, no completion email reaches anyone including the owner, and no `EMAIL_SENT` rows are written, because those are written after the send.

The download link is not the missing piece. The completion email template already renders a Download button, pointing at `/sign/{token}/complete` for recipients and at the team document page for the owner. That page already serves the sealed PDF through `EnvelopeDownloadDialog`. Delivery by link works today.

This overlaps #2766, which asks for the same capability from a confidentiality position. I hold that position too: some organisations cannot put executed documents into email at all. I filed separately because a provider size cap is a failure rather than a preference, it is specific to self-hosted deployments, and it did not come up in that thread.

## Additional Information & Alternatives (optional)

This is a proposal, not a specification. Order reflects what would help me soonest:

1. A self-hosted environment variable, for example `NEXT_PRIVATE_SMTP_MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE`. Unset preserves current behavior exactly. A positive value sets a byte cap above which the email sends the download link and no attachment. Zero never attaches. The comparison needs to run against the base64 encoded size, because a 20 MB PDF passes a raw 25 MB check and still fails at roughly 27 MB.
2. A per-document setting alongside the existing completion email toggles in `emailSettings`, defaulting to current behavior.
3. An organisation or team default for that setting, following the email preference inheritance already in place.

Items 2 and 3 are close to what #2766 asked for.

`packages/email/transports/mailchannels.ts:76-99` builds its API payload from `subject`, `text`, and `html` and never reads `mail.data.attachments`. Deployments on that transport already send completion emails with no attachment and no log line.

I have item 1 working on a fork and can finish all three. I am not opening a pull request, per CONTRIBUTING.md. Say the word and I will link the branch for you to take, adapt, or ignore.

I drafted this with AI assistance and verified the code references myself. I do not have access to OpenCode, so I am using Claude Code with your `.agents` skills and commands symlinked in.

### Feature Description/Problem

When provisioning new users via OIDC, Documenso creates a standalone user account with a personal workspace by default. There is currently no way to specify a default organization or team for newly provisioned SSO accounts to join automatically.

This creates both an administrative headache and a **security/brand-risk issue** in enterprise or self-hosted environments:
* **Brand / Security Risk:** Because a user provisioned via OIDC receives a personal workspace, they can create their own teams and start sending documents. These documents are issued from the company’s domain and signed using the instance’s configured signing certificate.
  * **Risk Scenario A:** An employee uses the company's self-hosted instance to run side-business operations or personal documents using corporate signing authority.
  * **Risk Scenario B:** A rogue or departing employee creates official-looking documents or contracts under the company's domain without organizational oversight.

Additionally, when attempting to automate user provisioning via the API, the current **REST API (v2)** lacks administrative endpoints for managing accounts, organizations, or team invitations.

### Proposed Solution

#### 1. OIDC Organization Assignment (Phased Roadmap?)

* **Phase 1 (Quick Fix / Short Term):**
  Add an environment variable (e.g., `NEXT_PRIVATE_OIDC_DEFAULT_TEAM_ID` or `NEXT_PRIVATE_OIDC_DEFAULT_ORG_ID`) that automatically places any user logged in via OIDC into a designated default team/organization upon JIT account creation.

* **Phase 2 (Medium Term):**
  Support **OIDC Group Claims Mapping**. Allow administrators to map incoming OIDC claim groups (e.g., `groups`, `roles`) to specific Documenso Teams automatically during login.

* **Phase 3 (Long Term):**
  Implement **SCIM 2.0** support to enable full identity-provider lifecycle management (creation, team mapping, and deprovisioning) from IdPs like Kanidm, Okta, Microsoft Entra, etc.

#### 2. Administrative REST API Endpoints

Expose public REST API endpoints (or global administrative API tokens) for platform and team management operations:
* `POST /api/v2/teams/{teamId}/invites` or `POST /api/v2/organization/invites` (Invite users to a team/organization)
* `GET /api/v2/users` / `GET /api/v2/teams` (Retrieve platform or team user listings)
* `DELETE /api/v2/teams/{teamId}/members/{userId}` (Remove members programmatically)

> **Note on Real-World Impact:**
> While administrative APIs are often treated as an "enterprise-only" feature, the lack of management endpoints heavily impacts small-to-medium teams, non-profits, and volunteer groups. 
> For instance, a regional non-profit with 50–100 members may need 15 distinct team spaces corresponding to local counties/districts, with 2–5 members assigned per district. Manually creating 15 teams and inviting dozens of users through the web UI consumes valuable administrative hours. Exposing basic team-management API endpoints allows simple orchestration tools (like n8n or Python scripts) to automate this setup.

### Additional Context

Context / Reproduction Steps
1. Configure environment variables for generic OIDC provider.
2. Log in with a new user through OIDC.
3. Observe that the user account is provisioned into an isolated personal workspace with no organizational bounding or team assignment.
4. Check API Documentation (v2) or attempt API calls for user/team provisioning; observe that all current endpoints are scoped exclusively to documents, templates, and envelopes.
---
### Additional Context
* **Documenso Version:** v2.18.0 / Self-hosted
* **Authentication Method:** OIDC via kanidm

### Issue Description

On the signing page, `CHECKBOX` and `RADIO` fields are positioned by their top/left corner only and the HTML widget keeps its intrinsic size (12 px circles/boxes stacked with a 4 px gap). The PDF renderer on the other hand (`packages/lib/universal/field-renderer/field-renderer.ts` → `calculateMultiItemPosition`) distributes the options evenly across the **full field height/width** (8 px padding, equal slots, item centred in its slot).

So what the recipient sees while signing never matches where the options end up in the exported PDF. This breaks a very common use case: placing a radio/checkbox field over **pre-printed option boxes** of a contract (e.g. "☐ I agree to start immediately / ☐ I want to wait for the withdrawal period"). In the PDF the circles land exactly in the boxes; on the signing page they are a small cluster at the top-left of the field, next to the first sentence only.

Root cause: `FieldContainerPortal` in `packages/ui/components/field/field.tsx` explicitly skips `height`/`width` for checkbox and radio fields:

```ts
const isCheckboxOrRadioField = field.type === 'CHECKBOX' || field.type === 'RADIO';
...
...(!isCheckboxOrRadioField
  ? { height: `${coords.height}px`, width: `${coords.width}px` }
  : { maxWidth: `${maxWidth}px` }),
```

Related: #2141 (closed) asked for resizable symbols; this report is about the signing page ignoring the field bounds altogether, which is what actually makes the options land in the wrong place.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Upload a PDF that has two printed option boxes on top of each other (a contract clause with "☐ option A" / "☐ option B").
2. Add one radio field with two options and resize it so that it spans both boxes (top of the field at the top of box A, bottom at the bottom of box B). The editor preview shows one circle per box.
3. Send the document and open the signing link.
4. Compare with the completed PDF after signing.

### Expected Behavior

The signing page renders the radio/checkbox field with the same geometry as the PDF renderer: the field container has the stored width/height, every option gets an equal slot across the field (vertical or horizontal according to `fieldMeta.direction`), the item is centred in its slot – so the circles sit in the printed boxes, exactly like in the completed PDF.

### Current Behavior

The widget is a fixed-size block at the top-left corner of the field (both circles next to option A, nothing next to option B), while the completed PDF shows the circles inside the boxes.

Measured with Playwright (Chromium, 1400 px viewport, page rendered at 828 px width) on v2.18.0 for a required 2-option radio field spanning two boxes:

| | Field container on the signing page | Option circles (y) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before (v2.18.0) | 82 × 40 px, intrinsic widget size | 484 px / 504 px – both above box A |
| with the fix below | 124 × 240 px = stored field bounds | 438 px / 550 px – centred on box A and box B, matching the PDF export |

### Screenshots (optional)

Before (v2.18.0):

![signing page before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nitrompu/documenso/assets/field-bounds-screenshots/screenshots/signing-page-before.png)

After (with the fix):

![signing page after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nitrompu/documenso/assets/field-bounds-screenshots/screenshots/signing-page-after.png)

### Proposed fix (tested)

Since external PRs are currently not accepted I am filing this as an issue; the change is small and self-contained (4 files, +52/−41 lines) and ready as a commit on top of `main`:

- Commit: https://github.com/nitrompu/documenso/commit/45681de6f37906d677a9832ca2a13fbdbe408706
- Branch: https://github.com/nitrompu/documenso/tree/fix/signing-checkbox-radio-field-bounds

1. `packages/ui/components/field/field.tsx` – `FieldContainerPortal` applies `height`/`width` to every field type (the `useElementBounds`/`maxWidth` special case goes away).
2. `apps/remix/app/components/general/document-signing/document-signing-radio-field.tsx` – the `RadioGroup` becomes `flex h-full w-full gap-0 py-2` + `flex-col`/`flex-row` (from `direction`), each option `flex min-h-3 flex-1 items-center`, items `shrink-0`.
3. `apps/remix/app/components/general/document-signing/document-signing-checkbox-field.tsx` – same layout for the checkbox widget.
4. `packages/ui/primitives/document-flow/field-content.tsx` – same layout for the read-only preview so document view and signing page agree.

Edge cases considered:

- Fields smaller than the widget needs (legacy documents): slots have `min-h-3`, so the widget overflows the container downwards like before instead of squeezing the items – no worse than today, and the PDF export already behaves the same way.
- `direction: 'horizontal'` keeps working (row layout, one slot per option, matching the PDF renderer's horizontal branch).
- Empty option labels (`empty-value-*` / `""`), the optional label above the field and the tooltips are unchanged.

Testing: `biome check` on the changed files is clean (the only warning, unused `targetSigner`, is pre-existing); production image built with `docker/Dockerfile` from v2.18.0 + this commit, deployed on our self-hosted instance, signing page verified as shown above. Happy to open the PR if you want to take it.

It is frequently not visible at all, so the signer cannot complete the field without first pinching back out to 100%.

The dialog is position: fixed, which is resolved against the layout viewport. Pinch zoom only moves the visual viewport, so the centered dialog is placed relative to the full unzoomed page and lands outside the region the signer is currently looking at. Because the whole view is magnified, it also appears enlarged. This affects every field type that opens this dialog, since they all use the shared packages/ui/primitives/dialog.tsx primitive (confirmed in apps/remix/app/components/general/document-signing/document-signing-text-field.tsx and its sibling field components).


### Steps to Reproduce

Self-hosted Documenso 2.17.0 (Docker).
Add a text field (or date/name/dropdown field) to a document and send it for signing.
Open the signing link on an Android phone in Chrome.
Pinch-zoom into the document to read or reach the field.
Tap the field to enter a value.


### Expected Behavior

The field input dialog appears within the currently visible (zoomed) region, correctly sized and aligned, so the signer can enter the value without changing zoom.


### Current Behavior

The dialog opens position: fixed relative to the layout viewport, so while the page is pinch-zoomed it renders outside the visible region and appears magnified and misaligned, often not visible at all. The signer has to pinch back out to 100% to locate and use it.

Relevant DOM (from device inspection): the portal wrapper is <div class="fixed inset-0 z-[1000] flex justify-center sm:items-center items-start"> and the dialog is <div role="dialog" class="... fixed z-50 grid w-full ... sm:max-w-lg sm:rounded-lg rounded-b-xl">.

Possible fix directions: while the dialog is open, track window.visualViewport (scale/offsetLeft/offsetTop) and position the dialog within the visible region, or reset pinch zoom to 1 when a field dialog opens. Both keep the fix at the shared dialog primitive so all field types benefit.

### Issue Description

`normalizePdf` refuses every PDF that carries an encryption dictionary. That test is broader than the problem it was added for, and it blocks a large, common class of documents: government forms.

Most agency forms (CRA, IRS, and others) ship with owner-password encryption. The user password is empty, so the file opens in any reader with no prompt and does not look encrypted to the person uploading it. Only the permission flags are set. Documenso refuses these files, and the person uploading sees "The document is encrypted" for a document they were never asked a password for.

`packages/lib/server-only/pdf/normalize-pdf.ts`:

```ts
if (pdfDoc.isEncrypted) {
  throw new AppError('INVALID_DOCUMENT_FILE', {
    message: 'The document is encrypted',
  });
}
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Download Canada Revenue Agency form AUT-01, "Authorize a Representative for Offline Access", from canada.ca. Any owner-password-protected agency form reproduces this.
2. Open it in any PDF reader. It opens with no password prompt.
3. Upload it to Documenso as a new document.
4. The upload is refused with "The document is encrypted".

The file's properties:

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Encryption | AES-128, revision 4 |
| User password | empty |
| Authenticated as | user |
| `modify` permission | false |
| `assemble` permission | false |
| Pages | 4 |
| AcroForm fields | 42 |

`PDF.load` opens it without a password and `isAuthenticated` is true. The document is fully readable. It is refused for the flag alone.

### Expected Behavior

An encrypted PDF that Documenso can actually open should be accepted. A file that genuinely needs a password should be refused with a message that says so, rather than the same opaque error for both cases.

### Current Behavior

Both cases produce "The document is encrypted", and neither is accepted.

**Why the obvious fix does not work.** `removeProtection()` looks like the answer, but `PDF.load` authenticates with the empty user password, which yields user-level access without `modify`:

```
loaded: isEncrypted=true isAuthenticated=true hasOwnerAccess=false
removeProtection() -> PermissionDeniedError:
  "Cannot remove protection: requires owner access or modify permission"
```

`PDF.merge` is not an answer either; it preserves the encryption dictionary.

**What does work.** Rebuilding the pages into a fresh document drops the encryption dictionary without needing owner access:

```ts
pdfDoc = await pdfDoc.extractPages([...Array(pdfDoc.getPageCount()).keys()]);
```

Verified on the AUT-01 with `@libpdf/core` 0.4.0:

- `isEncrypted` false afterwards.
- 4 pages in, 4 pages out.
- All 9,926 characters of extracted text identical to the original.
- Rendered pages visually unchanged, every filled value intact.
- Interactive form fields drop from 42 to 0.

The last point is the constraint. `extractPages` and `copyPagesFrom` both return a document with no AcroForm, so the rebuild is only safe where the form was going to be flattened anyway.

**Suggested shape:**

```ts
if (pdfDoc.isEncrypted) {
  // Needs a real password. Nothing to be done, but say which problem it is.
  if (!pdfDoc.isAuthenticated) {
    throw new AppError('INVALID_DOCUMENT_FILE', {
      message: 'This PDF is password protected. Re-save it without a password and try again.',
    });
  }

  // Rebuilding drops the AcroForm, so it is only safe when the form was
  // going to be flattened anyway.
  if (!shouldFlattenForm) {
    throw new AppError('INVALID_DOCUMENT_FILE', {
      message: 'This PDF is encrypted, and removing the encryption would discard its form fields.',
    });
  }

  pdfDoc = await pdfDoc.extractPages([...Array(pdfDoc.getPageCount()).keys()]);
}
```

In current `main`, `flattenForm` is false only when the envelope is a `TEMPLATE`. Every other path already flattens, so the rebuild costs those paths nothing.

**Related history:**

- #1130 added the check because a signed encrypted document could not be sealed. That is a real problem, but the blanket `isEncrypted` test overshoots it: an owner-password form with an empty user password can be read, rebuilt, and sealed normally.
- #1371 is a user hitting the same opaque failure and asking for a message that explains it. It was closed, and the message is still "The document is encrypted".
- #2853 moves toward importing AcroForm widgets as Documenso fields rather than flattening them. That interacts with this: if a path stops flattening, it also stops being safe to rebuild, so the `shouldFlattenForm` gate above should follow whatever that PR settles on.

**Secondary observation**, possibly a `@libpdf/core` bug rather than a Documenso one, but it showed up while testing this. For a PDF with a genuine user password, loaded without that password:

```
isEncrypted=true isAuthenticated=false
removeProtection() -> succeeds, and saving emits an unencrypted file
```

`extractPages` behaves the same way. A document that was never authenticated should not be decryptable. Documenso is not currently exposed to this because it rejects before reaching either call, but any fix here should check `isAuthenticated` explicitly rather than relying on those methods to refuse.

### Screenshots (optional)

Not applicable. The failure is a server-side rejection, and the reproduction above is deterministic.

### Operating System [e.g., Windows 10]

Linux (Docker, self-hosted). Reproduced independently on macOS.

### Browser [e.g., Chrome, Firefox]

Not browser-dependent. The rejection happens server-side in `normalizePdf`.

### Version [e.g., 2.13.0]

2.13.0, with `@libpdf/core` 0.4.0. The check is unchanged on `main` as of this writing.

### Issue Description

**Root cause (confirmed in source):**
On /organisation/invite/$token, when the loader determines userExists === false for the invited email, the rendered "Create account" button links to:

/signup#email=${encodeURIComponent(email)}

This link does not carry the invite token forward in any form (query param, redirect param, session storage, etc.). Once the user navigates away to /signup, the token is lost. Registration and email verification proceed through the normal signup flow, which has no knowledge of the pending invite.

The invite is only accepted when the user lands on /organisation/invite/$token again while authenticated and isSessionUserTheInvitedUser evaluates true (matching by email against the now-existing User row) — this triggers the trpc.organisation.member.invite.accept mutation client-side. Since nothing redirects the user back to that URL after signup, this normally never happens unless the invite email is clicked a second time.

**Suggested fix:**

- Append the invite token to the signup link, e.g. /signup?invitationToken={token}#email={email}, and have the signup flow persist it (query param survives redirect, or store in a short-lived cookie/session).

- After successful registration + email verification, redirect back to /organisation/invite/{token} automatically (or call the accept-invite mutation server-side directly) so the membership is created without requiring a second click on the original email link.

**Workaround (documented for our users in the meantime):**
After creating the account and verifying the email, click the original invite link from the email a second time. The token doesn't expire while the invite is PENDING, so no "Resend" from the admin is required.

### Steps to Reproduce

Org admin invites a new email address that has no existing Documenso account.
Invitee opens the invite email and clicks the invite link (/organisation/invite/{token}).
Since no account exists yet, the page shows a "Create account" button. Invitee clicks it.
Invitee completes signup and verifies their email address (email/password flow).
Invitee logs in and checks the organisation — they are not a member. Admin's invite list still shows the invitation as PENDING.

### Expected Behavior

After completing signup (triggered directly from the invite page) and verifying the email, the invitee should automatically become a member of the inviting organisation, or at minimum be redirected back to complete the invite acceptance.

### Current Behavior

The invite silently stays PENDING indefinitely. The only way to complete it is for the admin to click "Resend" and the invitee to click the invite link again while logged in — at which point it works.

### Issue Description

#3290 fixed the create path; the update path has the same hole. `updateEnvelopeFields` (`packages/lib/server-only/field/update-envelope-fields.ts`) validates recipients, item ownership, and the field-meta/type match, but never inspects the `fieldMeta` it persists — and the update replaces the meta wholesale (`fieldMeta: updateData.fieldMeta`), so:

- `POST /api/v2/envelope/field/update-many` with `fieldMeta: {"type": "text", "required": true, "readOnly": true}` returns 200 and persists the forbidden combination;
- a field created legal (`required: true`) can be flipped illegal in one update that supplies `readOnly: true` in its replacement meta.

The documented rules are the same five Field Types pages quoted in #3290, and the runtime consequences are identical: the signer-facing validation error the sender never sees.

### Cause

The per-field loop runs exactly four checks (field exists, recipient exists, `canRecipientFieldsBeModified`, meta/type match) and writes `updateData.fieldMeta` straight to `tx.field.update`. No call to the configuration validators, which after #3293 exist as a reusable `validateFieldMetaConfiguration`.

### Suggested fix

Run `validateFieldMetaConfiguration(fieldType, field.fieldMeta)` in the same loop — the effective type is already computed (`field.type || originalField.type`), and only the *provided* meta needs validating, because the update replaces it wholesale (an omitted meta keeps the stored one, per #3286/#3289). Reject with `AppError(AppErrorCode.INVALID_REQUEST)` so the API answers 400, mirroring #3290's create-path fix.

#### Suggested labels

`type: bug`

Found while reviewing #3293's coverage; the same audit reasoning as #3290 applies.

items.body:
### Issue Description

Two published pages state that the Assistant role is only available when sequential signing is enabled, and one of them lists "Be used in parallel signing mode" under what an assistant cannot do. The v2 API does not enforce it. On an envelope whose `documentMeta.signingOrder` is `PARALLEL`, `POST /api/v2/envelope/recipient/create-many` with `role: ASSISTANT` returns 200 and persists the recipient. There is no refusal of any kind.

The result is not only a contract violation. With `signingOrder` PARALLEL, `send-document.ts` notifies every recipient at once, so signers can sign before the assistant has pre-filled anything, which is the guarantee the restriction exists to protect. And the assistant's own view is broken: `getRecipientsForAssistant` and `getFieldsForToken` filter with `signingOrder: { gte: assistant.signingOrder ?? 0 }`, which is NULL-false in SQL for the null `signingOrder` an API-created parallel recipient carries, so the assistant sees an empty recipient list and none of the fields they are supposed to pre-fill.

#### Documentation

https://docs.documenso.com/docs/concepts/recipient-roles, Assistant tab:

> Assistants can prepare the document by pre-filling fields on behalf of other signers. This role is only available when sequential signing is enabled.

> **What they cannot do:**
>
> * Sign on behalf of other recipients
> * Submit the document as complete
> * Be used in parallel signing mode

> The Assistant role requires sequential signing to be enabled. You cannot use this role when recipients sign in parallel.

https://docs.documenso.com/docs/users/documents/add-recipients:

> The Assistant role is only available when sequential signing is enabled.

> Sequential signing is required to use the Assistant role. Assistants must act before the signers whose fields they pre-fill.

`add-recipients` frames the rule as an editor toggle, but `recipient-roles` states it as a property of the role itself, so it binds the API too.

#### Cause

`createEnvelopeRecipients` runs exactly one per-recipient role assertion: https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65/packages/lib/server-only/recipient/create-envelope-recipients.ts#L62-L97. The loop calls `assertCompatibleRecipientRole({ signatureLevel: envelope.signatureLevel, role: recipient.role })`, which keys on signature level alone and only rejects ASSISTANT on AES/QES (TSP) envelopes, returning early for SES, the default. Nothing on the path reads `envelope.documentMeta.signingOrder`, and no PARALLEL or SEQUENTIAL comparison exists anywhere in the file. The request schema accepts `z.nativeEnum(RecipientRole)` with no refinement and the route adds nothing.

The rule lives only in the two editor forms: `packages/ui/primitives/document-flow/add-signers.tsx` and `apps/remix/app/components/general/envelope-editor/envelope-editor-recipient-form.tsx` both intercept a role change to ASSISTANT while signingOrder is PARALLEL, flip the form to SEQUENTIAL and toast "You cannot add assistants when signing order is disabled". Grepping `ASSISTANT` across `packages/lib/server-only` and `packages/trpc/server` finds no signing-order check at all. The role and its client-side-only enforcement arrived together in #1588 (2025-02-01, "feat: assistant role"); the v2 route that exposes the gap is #2105 (2025-11-07, "feat: add envelopes api").

Still present at today's head, `75330166cc` (v2.17.0): https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/75330166cc00b29c14399bc2e391e4b4d8080c00/packages/lib/server-only/recipient/create-envelope-recipients.ts#L62-L97. The file and both doc pages are byte-identical to the tested v2.16.0.

The codebase already has the shape of the fix: `packages/lib/server-only/signature-level/` holds `assert-compatible-recipient-role.ts` and `assert-compatible-signing-order.ts`, two asserts called from this same service. A complete fix has to cover `update-envelope-recipients` and the envelope-meta path as well, since flipping an envelope back to PARALLEL while an ASSISTANT recipient exists reaches the same illegal state from the other side.

#### Suggested labels

`type: bug`

#### Related

- #2973, "Assistant (Form Filler) Must Always Act Before Signers Without Requiring Workflow Ordering" (open): argues the restriction should be dropped and the assistant made a role that always acts first. It does not report that the API accepts the combination. There are two acceptable resolutions to this issue and they point in opposite directions: enforce the documented rule server-side, or change the docs and the workflow the way #2973 asks. Either settles it; the current state, where the docs forbid it and the API allows it, does not.
- #2995 (closed unmerged, 2026-06-22): the community PR for #2973, which would have removed the UI restriction and reordered notification and turn logic. Because it never landed, the docs still forbid the combination while the API still allows it.
- #1588 (merged): origin of the role and of the UI-only enforcement.

Found by TrueCourse running the product's own documentation against a live instance; the full transcript (requests, responses, server log) is available on request.

### Steps to Reproduce

Build tested: v2.16.0 (tag `v2.16.0`, `3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65`), built and run from source: `npm ci`, `npx turbo run build --filter=@documenso/remix`, `npm run start -w @documenso/remix`, against Postgres 17, with `NEXT_PRIVATE_JOBS_PROVIDER=local` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_TRANSPORT=database`. Every call carries a team API token: `Authorization: <token>`. Ids below are from the recorded run.

1. Create an envelope and leave its signing order at the default (`documentMeta.signingOrder` is `PARALLEL` for an envelope created this way):

   `POST /api/v2/envelope/use`, `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=tcguard`, payload part `{"envelopeId":"<template envelope id>","externalId":"tcref-assistant-cb1cebb0ee"}`
   200, `{"id":"envelope_uanynwhkkxelvdtm","recipients":[]}`

   `GET /api/v2/envelope/envelope_uanynwhkkxelvdtm` confirms `"documentMeta":{"signingOrder":"PARALLEL", ...}`.

2. Add an assistant:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/recipient/create-many
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_uanynwhkkxelvdtm","data":[{"email":"tcref-asst-cb1cebb0ee@documenso.test","name":"TCRef Assistant","role":"ASSISTANT"}]}
   ```

   200, and the recipient is persisted.

Re-tested live on v2.17.0 (75330166cc, 2026-08-19): still reproduces. ASSISTANT was accepted with 200 both on the default envelope, whose documentMeta.signingOrder reads PARALLEL, and on one set to PARALLEL explicitly, and the created recipient carries signingOrder: null, the value that makes the assistant's own document view come back empty.

### Expected Behavior

The call is refused and no recipient is created, because the envelope signs in parallel. No doc page publishes a status code for this refusal; `AppErrorCode.INVALID_BODY` maps to 400 and is what the sibling `assertCompatibleRecipientRole` already throws for the AES/QES case. The point of this report is that there is no refusal at all, not that the status code is wrong.

### Current Behavior

Step 2 returns HTTP 200 with the assistant created:

```json
{"data":[{"envelopeId":"envelope_uanynwhkkxelvdtm","role":"ASSISTANT","readStatus":"NOT_OPENED","signingStatus":"NOT_SIGNED","sendStatus":"NOT_SENT","id":349,"email":"tcref-asst-cb1cebb0ee@documenso.test","name":"TCRef Assistant","token":"<token>","documentDeletedAt":null,"expired":null,"expiresAt":null,"expirationNotifiedAt":null,"signedAt":null,"authOptions":{"accessAuth":[],"actionAuth":[]},"signingOrder":null,"rejectionReason":null}]}
```

The server log records `envelope.recipient.createMany` running normally, with no warning; stderr is empty.

Provenance of the PARALLEL claim: this particular recorded scenario did not read the envelope back between step 1 and step 2, so the `PARALLEL` signing order comes from sibling runs in the same session, where every envelope minted from a template this way carries `documentMeta.signingOrder: "PARALLEL"` (30 of the 31 signing-order readings across the session are PARALLEL, the one exception being an envelope explicitly set to SEQUENTIAL). The GET in step 1 above makes that check part of the reproduction.

Note `"signingOrder": null` on the created row: that is the value the assistant's own queries then filter against with `gte`, which is why the assistant's recipient and field lists come back empty.

### Operating System [e.g., Windows 10]

n/a (API, self-hosted from source)

### Browser [e.g., Chrome, Firefox]

n/a (API)

### Version [e.g., 2.13.0]

2.16.0 (tested; tag `v2.16.0` = `3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65`), re-checked in source against 2.17.0 (`75330166cc00b29c14399bc2e391e4b4d8080c00`), where the culprit file and both doc pages are byte-identical.

- [x] I have included the relevant environment information.

### Issue Description

The Field Types page states, in five separate Rules lists, that a field cannot be both required and read-only at the same time. The v2 create path never validates `fieldMeta` at all, so `POST /api/v2/envelope/field/create-many` accepts `{"required": true, "readOnly": true}` with a 200 and persists the field with the forbidden meta echoed back. The rules are enforced elsewhere in the codebase, on the editor's `setFieldsForDocument` path and again at signing time, so a configuration created over the API surfaces later as a signer-facing error the sender never saw.

#### Documentation

https://docs.documenso.com/docs/concepts/field-types, Text > Rules:

> * A field cannot be both required and read-only at the same time
> * A read-only field must have a default text value (it cannot be empty)

The same sentence appears in the Rules lists for Number, Radio, Checkbox and Dropdown, so the page states it as a product-wide invariant, and its Related section points at "Fields API - Programmatically add fields via the API".

#### Cause

The only validation the v2 create path runs is the block commented "Field validation and placeholder resolution": https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65/packages/lib/server-only/field/create-envelope-fields.ts#L138-L245. It checks three things: that `envelopeItemId` belongs to the envelope, that `recipientId` exists, and that `canRecipientFieldsBeModified` allows new fields. It never inspects `fieldMeta`, and the values go straight to `field.createManyAndReturn` as `fieldMeta: field.fieldMeta`. The schema does not catch it either: `ZBaseFieldMeta` declares `required` and `readOnly` as two independent optional booleans with no cross-field refine, so the combination parses cleanly.

The validators for exactly these documented rules already exist in `packages/lib/advanced-fields-validation/`: `validate-text.ts` pushes "A field cannot be both read-only and required", with the same check in `validate-number.ts`, `validate-radio.ts`, `validate-checkbox.ts` and `validate-dropdown.ts`. They are called server-side from `packages/lib/server-only/field/set-fields-for-document.ts:136-195` and `set-fields-for-template.ts`. `createEnvelopeFields` simply does not call them.

The gap predates the envelope refactor: the pre-envelope `create-document-fields.ts` did not validate `fieldMeta` either, so #2025 (2025-10-14, "feat: add envelopes") carried an existing hole onto the v2 API rather than regressing working code. The doc page that promises the rules was added by #2460 (2026-02-27, "feat: docs v2") and has not changed since.

Still present at today's head, `75330166cc` (v2.17.0): https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/75330166cc00b29c14399bc2e391e4b4d8080c00/packages/lib/server-only/field/create-envelope-fields.ts#L138-L245. The create path, the shared validators and the doc page are all byte-identical to the tested v2.16.0.

Two scope facts: the same unvalidated service also backs the v1 `POST /document/field/create-many`, so this is not v2-only; and a fix should throw `AppError(AppErrorCode.INVALID_REQUEST)` so the API answers 400, rather than the bare `new Error(errors.join(', '))` the `setFields` path throws today, which surfaces as a 500 even where the rules are enforced.

#### Suggested labels

`type: bug`

#### Related

- #3152 (open) and #3122 (open): two community PRs inside `validateNumberField`, the shared validator this create path never calls. Neither causes nor fixes this, but both show the community treats `packages/lib/advanced-fields-validation` as the home of these rules.
- #3224 (open), "fix: don't create a field on top of an identical one": another change on this same create path, adding a duplicate-position guard and no `fieldMeta` validation. Worth considering together.

### Issue Description

The lifecycle page says a rejection moves the document to Rejected immediately and that other pending recipients can no longer act on it. Neither holds at the moment the rejection returns. The rejection handler commits the recipient row and an audit log and nothing else; the document-level flip to `REJECTED` is written only by the asynchronous `internal.seal-document` job, after the whole PDF pipeline has run. The very next `GET /api/v2/envelope/{id}` still reports `"status": "PENDING"`.

The stale read is the visible half. The harm is the other half: every guard that stops the rest of the signing flow keys off `envelope.status === PENDING`. `sign-field-with-token` and `complete-document-with-token` check only that plus the acting recipient's own signing status, so for the whole window the other recipients can still sign or reject a document the product has already cancelled by email, since `send.document.cancelled.emails` is queued by the rejection request itself. If the seal job fails, and it demonstrably does (see #2921, #3092, #3191), the window never closes: the sweep job retries only between 15 minutes and 6 hours after the last recipient action and gives up after that.

#### Documentation

https://docs.documenso.com/docs/concepts/document-lifecycle, "Rejected":

> If you enable document rejection in settings, recipients can reject instead of signing. When any recipient rejects:
>
> * The document immediately moves to **Rejected** state
> * Other pending recipients can no longer act on the document
> * The document owner is notified

#### Cause

`rejectDocumentOnBehalfOf` commits exactly two rows in its transaction, the recipient (`signedAt`, `signingStatus: REJECTED`, `rejectionReason`) and a `DOCUMENT_RECIPIENT_REJECTED` audit log, then fires three jobs and returns: https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65/packages/lib/server-only/document/reject-document-on-behalf-of.ts#L115-L177. It never touches `Envelope.status`; the only `DocumentStatus` reference in the file is the precondition `if (envelope.status !== DocumentStatus.PENDING)`.

The single writer of `DocumentStatus.REJECTED` in production code is `packages/lib/jobs/definitions/internal/seal-document.handler.ts`, which computes `finalEnvelopeStatus = isRejected ? REJECTED : COMPLETED` and writes it only after loading every envelope item's PDF, stamping the rejection, generating the certificate and audit-log PDFs, signing and uploading. With the default local job provider that job is dispatched over HTTP and explicitly not awaited (`packages/lib/jobs/client/local.ts` races the fetch against a 150 ms timeout), so the mutation returns long before the status changes.

The recipient-token path `reject-document-with-token.ts` has the identical shape, so this is the design of rejection rather than an API-only slip. The public API surface came with #3007 (2026-06-22, "feat: add API endpoint to reject documents on behalf of recipients"); the async design dates to #1472 (2024-11-14, "feat: signature rejection").

Still present at today's head, `75330166cc` (v2.17.0): https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/75330166cc00b29c14399bc2e391e4b4d8080c00/packages/lib/server-only/document/reject-document-on-behalf-of.ts#L115-L177. Both culprit files and the doc page are byte-identical to the tested v2.16.0.

Fix shape: write `Envelope.status = REJECTED` and the `DOCUMENT_REJECTED` webhook inside the same transaction that flips the recipient, and let the seal job produce only the stamped PDF. That closes the read-after-write gap, makes the "other recipients can no longer act" guard effective immediately, and removes the dependency of a terminal legal state on a PDF pipeline that can fail. If the asynchronous design is intended instead, the docs should say the status settles after sealing and point integrators at the `DOCUMENT_REJECTED` webhook, the way `developers/examples/common-workflows` already polls for a terminal status.

One thing that already works correctly and is worth documenting either way: recipient-level truth is immediate. The same GET payload already shows the rejecting recipient as `REJECTED` with the reason, so an integration can read the rejection off the recipient array before the envelope agrees.

#### Suggested labels

`type: bug`

#### Related

- #3191, "Rejecting an AES/QES envelope is a dead end: status never becomes REJECTED and cannot be recovered" (open since 2026-08-13, no comments): names the same single-writer root cause, but is scoped to the TSP/CSC case where the seal handler throws so the flip never happens at all. The ordinary non-TSP lag reported here is not covered by it.
- #3180, "Recipients who already signed can still reject, destroying their own signature" (open): a second missing guard on the same rejection path.
- #2921 and #3092 (open): two ways the seal job dies, leaving the envelope in PENDING forever.
- #2215 (closed): the completion twin, fixed with the sweep rather than a synchronous status write.
- #2563 (merged 2026-03-05): the seal-document sweep, the project's own mitigation for this class of stall; its query explicitly matches "any recipient has REJECTED". It runs 15 minutes to 6 hours after the last recipient action, so it cannot make "immediately" true.
- #3234 (closed unmerged, 2026-08-18): would have made the sweep cadence configurable, so that window is still fixed.

Found by TrueCourse running the product's own documentation against a live instance; the full transcript (requests, responses, server log) is available on request.

### Steps to Reproduce

Build tested: v2.16.0 (tag `v2.16.0`, `3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65`), built and run from source: `npm ci`, `npx turbo run build --filter=@documenso/remix`, `npm run start -w @documenso/remix`, against Postgres 17, with `NEXT_PRIVATE_JOBS_PROVIDER=local`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_TRANSPORT=database` and `NEXT_PRIVATE_SIGNING_TRANSPORT=local`. Every call carries a team API token: `Authorization: <token>`. Ids below are from the recorded run.

1. Create an envelope from a template: `POST /api/v2/envelope/use`, `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=tcguard`, payload part `{"envelopeId":"<template envelope id>","externalId":"tcref-reject-b99cc338a5"}`. 200, `{"id":"envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm","recipients":[]}`.

2. Add two signers, so the effect on a bystander is observable:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/recipient/create-many
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm","data":[{"email":"tcref-declines-b99cc338a5@documenso.test","name":"TCRef Decliner","role":"SIGNER"},{"email":"tcref-other-b99cc338a5@documenso.test","name":"TCRef Other","role":"SIGNER"}]}
   ```

   200, recipients `360` and `361`.

3. Give each a signature field:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/field/create-many
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm","data":[{"type":"SIGNATURE","recipientId":"360","page":1,"positionX":10,"positionY":70,"width":20,"height":5},{"type":"SIGNATURE","recipientId":"361","page":1,"positionX":10,"positionY":80,"width":20,"height":5}]}
   ```

   200.

4. Send it: `POST /api/v2/envelope/distribute` with `{"envelopeId":"envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm","meta":{"distributionMethod":"NONE"}}`. 200. (`NONE` only removes the need for a mail server.)

5. Reject on the first recipient's behalf:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/recipient/360/reject
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm","recipientId":"360","reason":"tcref declined b99cc338a5"}
   ```

   200, recipient 360 comes back `"signingStatus":"REJECTED"`, `"rejectionReason":"tcref declined b99cc338a5"`, `"signedAt":"2026-08-14T20:05:31.134Z"`. The server log shows the request firing `internal.seal-document`, `send.signing.rejected.emails` and `send.document.cancelled.emails`.

6. Read the envelope back immediately: `GET /api/v2/envelope/envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm`. 200.

Re-tested live on v2.17.0 (75330166cc, 2026-08-19): still reproduces. Reject returned 200 with signingStatus REJECTED on the recipient, but the envelope still read PENDING at 12 ms and at 112 ms after that 200, flipping to REJECTED at 52 ms in one run and 638 ms in another.

### Expected Behavior

Step 6 reports `"status": "REJECTED"`, and from step 5 onward recipient 361 can no longer sign or reject.

### Current Behavior

Step 6 returns `"status": "PENDING"` with `completedAt: null`, while the embedded recipients already read `360: REJECTED` and `361: NOT_SIGNED`:

```json
{"internalVersion":2,"type":"DOCUMENT","status":"PENDING","id":"envelope_dswotmftyonlisrm","secondaryId":"document_367","externalId":"tcref-reject-b99cc338a5","completedAt":null,"documentMeta":{"signingOrder":"PARALLEL","distributionMethod":"NONE", ...},"recipients":[{"role":"SIGNER","signingStatus":"REJECTED","id":360,"email":"tcref-declines-b99cc338a5@documenso.test","signedAt":"2026-08-14T20:05:31.134Z","rejectionReason":"tcref declined b99cc338a5", ...},{"role":"SIGNER","signingStatus":"NOT_SIGNED","id":361,"email":"tcref-other-b99cc338a5@documenso.test","signedAt":null,"rejectionReason":null, ...}], ...}
```

Step 5 took 299 ms and step 6 took 205 ms, so the read happened roughly 200 to 400 ms after the rejection. The cancellation emails to the owner and to recipient 361 had already been queued at that point.

Scope of the evidence: the transcript establishes only that the flip had not happened within that window; that the write is asynchronous, and therefore that the window has no documented bound, comes from the source, cited above. The recorded run stopped at this step, so the two follow-on assertions in the same flow (a rejected envelope refusing an update, and the second recipient being unable to reject) were never executed and carry no evidence either way.

### Issue Description

The Fields API documents `update-many` as a partial update: change one property of one field in a single request. In practice, any `update-many` call that does not resend the complete `fieldMeta` overwrites the stored configuration with the type's default metadata, behind a 200 that echoes the wiped state as though it were the update result. A TEXT field loses its label, placeholder, required flag and character limit; a RADIO field's option list becomes a single blank option, a CHECKBOX's becomes one blank unchecked option, a DROPDOWN's becomes a single "Option 1". There is no way to avoid it from the client side: `type` is the schema's union discriminator and is therefore mandatory on an update, so the default is always materialised. The documented update example, `{ id, type, pageY }`, is exactly the call that triggers it.

#### Documentation

https://docs.documenso.com/docs/developers/api/fields, "Update Fields":

> Update Fields [#update-fields]
>
> Update one or more fields in a single request.
>
> `POST /envelope/field/update-many`

and the response the page shows for that partial update:

```json
{
  "fields": [
    { "id": 101, "type": "SIGNATURE", "positionY": 85 },
    { "id": 102, "type": "DATE", "positionY": 85 }
  ]
}
```

Nothing on the page says a partial update discards the rest of the field's configuration.

#### Cause

`ZEnvelopeFieldAndMetaSchema` gives every fieldMeta-bearing member a create-time default: https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65/packages/lib/types/field-meta.ts#L403-L448. All ten members read `fieldMeta: Z<Type>FieldMeta.optional().default(FIELD_<TYPE>_META_DEFAULT_VALUES)` (SIGNATURE, INITIALS, NAME, EMAIL, DATE, TEXT, NUMBER, RADIO, CHECKBOX, DROPDOWN). The update route consumes that schema (`packages/trpc/server/envelope-router/envelope-fields/update-envelope-fields.types.ts:18`), so an omitted `fieldMeta` arrives at the service as the full default object rather than as `undefined`, and the service writes it unconditionally inside `tx.field.update`: https://github.com/documenso/documenso/blob/75330166cc00b29c14399bc2e391e4b4d8080c00/packages/lib/server-only/field/update-envelope-fields.ts#L136.

The defaults were introduced for create by #2181 (2025-11-12, "fix: add default values for envelope field meta"), which switched the update route's types from `ZFieldAndMetaSchema` to `ZEnvelopeFieldAndMetaSchema`; they are correct for create and wrong for update. The deprecated `/document/field/update-many` path is unaffected: its `ZUpdateFieldSchema` uses the plain `ZFieldAndMetaSchema` with no defaults.

Still present at today's head, `75330166cc` (v2.17.0): both `field-meta.ts` and `update-envelope-fields.ts` are byte-identical to the tested v2.16.0.

Fix shape: give the update route a schema whose `fieldMeta` is optional with no default, so an omitted `fieldMeta` leaves the column untouched, and leave create's defaults alone.

#### Suggested labels

`type: bug`

#### Related

- PR #3136 fixes the sibling defect on the same endpoint (the route validates `page` / `positionX` / `positionY` while the service reads `pageNumber` / `pageX` / `pageY`, so a move is a silent no-op). It covers the coordinate half only. Its current diff still forwards `fieldMeta: field.fieldMeta`, the zod-defaulted value, so with #3136 merged a move would work and the field's configuration would still be wiped. Merging it makes the endpoint look fixed while this defect stays.
- The audit log written by `diffFieldChanges` records the fieldMeta reset, so the loss is visible in the audit trail even though nothing surfaces it to the caller.

Found by TrueCourse running the published API docs against a live instance; the full transcript (requests, responses, server log) is available on request.

### Steps to Reproduce

Build tested: v2.16.0 (tag `v2.16.0`, `3cf2963cd03d8b24770b7490bdb20e596baa5d65`), built and run from source: `npm ci`, `npx turbo run build --filter=@documenso/remix`, `npm run start -w @documenso/remix`, against Postgres 17, with `NEXT_PRIVATE_JOBS_PROVIDER=local` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_TRANSPORT=database`. Every call carries a team API token: `Authorization: <token>`. Ids below are from the recorded run.

1. Create an envelope from a template: `POST /api/v2/envelope/use`, `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=tcguard`, payload part `{"envelopeId":"<template envelope id>","externalId":"tcref-fieldmove-4850ccfd5b"}`. 200, `{"id":"envelope_yroalbrelnoaxrmm","recipients":[]}`.

2. Add a recipient:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/recipient/create-many
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_yroalbrelnoaxrmm","data":[{"email":"tcref-4850ccfd5b@documenso.test","name":"TCRef Signer","role":"SIGNER"}]}
   ```

   200, recipient `id: 334`.

3. Create a configured TEXT field:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/field/create-many
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_yroalbrelnoaxrmm","data":[{"type":"TEXT","recipientId":"334","page":1,"positionX":10,"positionY":20,"width":20,"height":5,"fieldMeta":{"type":"text","label":"Job Title","placeholder":"Enter your job title","required":true,"characterLimit":40,"textAlign":"left"}}]}
   ```

   200, field `id: 300`, and the response echoes the meta back: `"fieldMeta":{"label":"Job Title","placeholder":"Enter your job title","required":true,"type":"text","characterLimit":40,"textAlign":"left"}`.

4. Update one property, sending no `fieldMeta`:

   ```
   POST /api/v2/envelope/field/update-many
   {"envelopeId":"envelope_yroalbrelnoaxrmm","data":[{"id":"300","type":"TEXT","positionY":60}]}
   ```

   200. The stored `fieldMeta` is now the TEXT defaults.

Re-tested live on v2.17.0 (75330166cc, 2026-08-19): still reproduces, unchanged. The same 200 replaced {label:'Job Title', placeholder:'Enter your job title', required:true, characterLimit:40, textAlign:'left'} with the text-type defaults.

### Expected Behavior

An `update-many` call that does not carry `fieldMeta` leaves the field's stored `fieldMeta` untouched. After step 4 the field still reads `{"label":"Job Title","placeholder":"Enter your job title","required":true,"type":"text","characterLimit":40,"textAlign":"left"}`.

### Current Behavior

Step 4 returns HTTP 200 and the stored configuration is gone:

```json
{"data":[{"envelopeId":"envelope_yroalbrelnoaxrmm","envelopeItemId":"envelope_item_iuruhhafmskdumud","type":"TEXT","id":300,"secondaryId":"cmstdmf0l0007y6r79fbzxeee","recipientId":334,"page":1,"positionX":"10","positionY":"20","width":"20","height":"5","customText":"","inserted":false,"fieldMeta":{"label":"","placeholder":"","required":false,"readOnly":false,"fontSize":12,"type":"text","text":"","textAlign":"left"},"documentId":343,"templateId":null}]}
```

That `fieldMeta` is byte-for-byte `FIELD_TEXT_META_DEFAULT_VALUES` (`packages/lib/types/field-meta.ts:302-312`). The response is built from the row after `prisma.field.update`, so it is what is persisted. The server log shows the `envelope.field.updateMany` call completing normally; stderr is empty.

The blast radius is all ten fieldMeta-bearing types. RADIO drops to `values: [{id: 1, checked: false, value: ''}]`, CHECKBOX to one blank unchecked option, DROPDOWN to `values: [{value: 'Option 1'}]` with an empty default, TEXT and NUMBER lose label, placeholder, default text or value, character limit and min/max. Every SDK generated from the v2 OpenAPI document inherits it.

The same response also shows the coordinate no-op that PR #3136 addresses: `positionY` is still `"20"` after a request that asked for 60.

### Issue Description

When the upload bucket has S3 Object Lock enabled, document sealing fails and documents remain stuck in PENDING after all recipients have signed.

The seal job retries three times and then gives up with:

[JOBS:task-...] Task failed InvalidRequest: Content-MD5 OR x-amz-checksum- HTTP header is required
for Put Object requests with Object Lock parameters
    at AwsRestXmlProtocol.handleError (/node_modules/@aws-sdk/core/dist-cjs/submodules/protocols/index.js)
[JOBS]: Job internal.seal-document failed BackgroundTaskExceededRetriesError: Task exceeded retries

S3 requires a Content-MD5 or x-amz-checksum-* header on any PutObject request that carries Object Lock parameters. packages/lib/universal/upload/providers/s3-provider.ts sets:

ts
requestChecksumCalculation: 'WHEN_REQUIRED',
responseChecksumValidation: 'WHEN_REQUIRED',

The in-code comment explains why — S3-compatible providers such as GarageHQ, MinIO and Backblaze B2 reject the AWS SDK's default CRC32 checksums with InvalidDigest. That is a reasonable default, but it is not overridable: because the value is set explicitly on the client, the standard AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION environment variable has no effect.

Uploads are unaffected because they use a presigned browser POST, which carries no Object Lock parameters. Only the server-side seal write fails.

### Steps to Reproduce

Configure NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_TRANSPORT=s3 against a real AWS S3 bucket
Enable Object Lock on that bucket with a default retention period
Create a document, send it, and have all recipients sign
Sealing fails; the document stays PENDING and appears under Admin → Unsealed Documents

### Expected Behavior

Sealing succeeds against buckets with Object Lock enabled, or the checksum behaviour is configurable so operators who need it can opt in without patching.

### Current Behavior

Make it configurable while keeping the current default, so third-party S3-compatible backends are unaffected:


requestChecksumCalculation:
  env('NEXT_PRIVATE_UPLOAD_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION') === 'WHEN_SUPPORTED'
    ? 'WHEN_SUPPORTED'
    : 'WHEN_REQUIRED',

## Summary

Documenso does not resolve an **inherited `/MediaBox`**. When a PDF declares its page size only on the `/Pages` node — which is valid per PDF 32000-1:2008 §7.7.3.4, where `MediaBox` is an inheritable page attribute — the page size falls back to US Letter. On A4 documents every placeholder-resolved field is then misplaced, and the offset grows with the distance from the page origin.

This affects `POST /envelope/field/create-many` with `placeholder`, and by the same mechanism anything else that maps coordinates onto the page.

## Evidence

Same page content, same placeholders, only the location of the `/MediaBox` differs:

| `/MediaBox` location | resolved column positions (mm) | row spacing (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| on `/Pages` only (inherited) | 15.6 · 54.5 · 93.4 · 132.3 · 166.3 | 26.5 |
| on each `/Page` (explicit) | 16.0 · 56.0 · 96.0 · 136.0 · 171.0 | 24.9 |
| **expected** | **16.0 · 56.0 · 96.0 · 136.0 · 171.0** | **24.9** |

The deviation in the inherited case is exactly the A4/Letter ratio:

```
x: measured 0.97250 … 0.97321   A4/Letter width  210 / 215.9 = 0.97267
y: measured 1.06292             A4/Letter height 297 / 279.4 = 1.06299
```

The source file is unambiguous — `pdfinfo` reports `Page size: 595.28 x 841.89 pts (A4)`, and the box is present, just one level up:

```
1 0 obj  /Type /Pages   /MediaBox [0 0 595.28 841.89]   ← inherited from here
3 0 obj  /Type /Page    (no /MediaBox)
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Generate an A4 PDF whose `/MediaBox` sits only on the `/Pages` node — fpdf2 does this by default when all pages share one size; other producers do the same.
2. Place `{{signature}}` at known positions, e.g. a grid at x = 15/55/95/135/170 mm, y = 20/45/…/195 mm.
3. `POST /document/create` (multipart) with one `SIGNER` recipient.
4. `POST /envelope/field/create-many`:
   ```json
   { "envelopeId": "…", "data": [
       { "recipientId": 1, "envelopeItemId": "…", "type": "SIGNATURE",
         "placeholder": "{{signature}}", "matchAll": true } ] }
   ```
5. Compare the resulting `positionX` / `positionY` with the placeholder positions from `pdftotext -bbox`.
6. Repeat with the same PDF after copying the `/MediaBox` onto each page — the offsets disappear.

## Side effect: fields are silently dropped

Of 50 placeholders in the grid, only **43** produced fields in the inherited case. The missing ones are the lowest rows: after the 1.063 stretch they exceed 279.4 mm and fall outside the assumed page. The API returns success, the fields are simply absent — so a document can be distributed with fewer signature fields than intended.

## Environment

- Documenso v2.16.0, self-hosted, `NEXT_PUBLIC_UPLOAD_TRANSPORT=database`
- Documents created via `POST /api/v2/document/create`, fields via `POST /api/v2/envelope/field/create-many`
- Source PDFs produced by fpdf2 2.8.x, A4, embedded TrueType subset

## Expected behaviour

When a page has no own `/MediaBox`, walk up the page tree and use the inherited one, as required by the specification. Falling back to US Letter silently produces wrong geometry for every A4 document, which is the default format outside North America.

## Note

Explicit coordinates (`page` / `positionX` / `positionY` / `width` / `height`) are placed correctly on the same file, so the regression is confined to the path that derives geometry from the page size.

## Workaround for producers

Write the `/MediaBox` into every `/Page` object instead of relying on inheritance. In fpdf2 this can be done before serialising:

```python
from fpdf.output import _dimensions_to_mediabox

for page in pdf.pages.values():
    if not page.media_box:
        page.media_box = _dimensions_to_mediabox(page.dimensions())
```
items.title: [Bug]: Inherited /MediaBox ignored — page size falls back to US Letter, misplacing placeholder fields on A4

### Describe the improvement you are suggesting in detail

In the Japanese locale, the product's core noun — document — is translated as 「ドキュメント」 in roughly half the UI and 「文書」 in the other half.

Counting every entry in `packages/lib/translations/ja/web.po` (3,099 entries, checked in full rather than sampled):

| Term | Entries |
| --- | --- |
| ドキュメント (dokyumento) | 284 |
| 文書 (bunsho) | 306 |

A Japanese user moving through one flow — upload, send, sign, complete — sees the thing they are signing change its name from screen to screen.

## 1. Same string, two translations

These msgids appear more than once (different contexts) and were translated independently:

| msgid | Translations found |
| --- | --- |
| `Document completed` | ドキュメントが完了しました / 文書が完了しました |
| `Document sent` | ドキュメントが送信されました / 文書を送信しました |
| `Document deleted` | ドキュメントが削除されました / 文書を削除しました |

Note the second axis of drift in `Document sent`: 「〜が送信されました」 vs 「〜を送信しました」 — passive vs active, so even the grammatical subject of the notification changes between contexts.

## 2. A second layer: the English source itself is inconsistent, and the Japanese followed it

| msgid (differs only in capitalization) | Japanese |
| --- | --- |
| `Document viewed` | ドキュメントが閲覧されました |
| `Document Viewed` | 文書が閲覧されました |
| `Document title` | 文書タイトル |
| `Document Title` | ドキュメントタイトル |

Two English casings, translated (apparently) by two different people, landed on opposite terms. Merging these msgids would fix both languages at once.

## 3. 140 entries are untranslated (empty msgstr)

They fall back to English inside the Japanese UI. User-facing examples:

- `Account Settings` — the entry point to settings
- - `<0>{organisationName}</0> does not have an active subscription. Please…`
- - - `<0>{organisationName}</0> has reached its member limit. Please contact…`
- - - - `{0} results`, `{totalVisibleCount} items`, `+{extraCount} more`
The subscription and member-limit messages are billing moments — the worst place to switch languages on a user.

## 4. 28 smaller inconsistent pairs

| English | Variants |
| --- | --- |
| Admin panel | 管理パネル / 管理画面 |
| Default value | デフォルト値 / 既定値 |
| Forgot password | パスワードをお忘れですか？ / パスワードをお忘れの方 |
| Invalid token | トークンが無効です / 無効なトークン |
| Delete | delete (untranslated) / 削除 |

## What is working well

Worth saying clearly: the signing-flow vocabulary is perfectly consistent — Signature is always 署名, Signer is always 署名者, Recipient is always 受信者. And 受信者 matches what DocuSign's Japanese UI uses, which is exactly right for a product positioned as the open-source DocuSign alternative. The individual translations are good; this is a glossary problem, not a translator problem.

### Additional Information & Alternatives (optional)

Suggested direction: standardize on 「ドキュメント」. DocuSign's Japanese UI uses ドキュメント for the files being signed, and users evaluating Documenso as the open-source DocuSign alternative arrive with that vocabulary. 文書 also reads as stiff/officialese in a SaaS UI. And since ドキュメント is already used in half the UI, the diff touches only the other half.

Related: #3044 affects how Japanese recipient names render, so Japanese users are hitting display issues on top of the terminology drift.

I am a native Japanese speaker and I do localization QA professionally. Happy to open a PR covering the ドキュメント unification, the 140 empty msgstrs, and the 28 smaller pairs — and if you would rather keep 文書, say the word and I will standardize in that direction instead.

### Feature Description

Currently, Documenso has no way to flag that a particular signer's signature must be witnessed by a third party as part of the signing workflow. Some legal document types - most notably UK property deeds - require a witness to observe the signing and countersign, and this witness requirement needs to be captured and enforced by the platform, not just handled as an out-of-band process.

### Use Case

In UK conveyancing, HM Land Registry's Practice Guide 82 (PG82) sets out the requirements for executing deeds electronically. For certain documents (e.g. mortgage deeds, TR1 transfers), the signatory's signature must be witnessed by an independent adult who is physically present, and the witness's name, address, and signature must also be captured on the document alongside identity verification of the signer (e.g. via SMS OTP).

### Proposed Solution

- A new recipient role of WITNESS, similar to how APPROVER/CC roles exist today.
- Ability to link a witness recipient to the specific signer they are witnessing (analogous to how DocuSign supports witnessFor on a recipient).
- A witness-specific signature/name/date field set, distinct from a standard signer's fields.
- Workflow enforcement so the witness can only complete their part after (or alongside, depending on config) the signer they're attached to, and the document isn't considered fully executed until both have signed.
- Audit log entries that reflect the witness relationship (e.g. "Witnessed by X for signer Y") for the completion certificate.

### Alternatives (optional)

Today, achieving this with Documenso requires manual workarounds — e.g. adding the witness as a second "signer" recipient with no structural link to the person they're witnessing, no enforcement that they sign in the correct order/relationship, and no distinct field/role type on the document to represent "witness for signer X."

### Issue Description

Webhook deliveries carry no stable identifier, so a consumer cannot deduplicate retries.

**`packages/lib/jobs/definitions/internal/execute-webhook.handler.ts:20-25`**
```js
const payloadData = { event, payload: data, createdAt: new Date().toISOString(), webhookEndpoint: url };
```
**`packages/lib/server-only/webhooks/execute-webhook-call.ts:38-41`** — headers are `Content-Type` and the secret only. No delivery id in the body, none in a header.

This matters because retries are real and intentional: `bullmq.ts:117,158` schedules with `attempts: DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES`, and the handler rethrows explicitly (`:44`) when a delivery fails. And `createdAt` is recomputed with `new Date()` **inside `run`**, so two attempts at the same event reach the consumer with **different bodies** and no stable field between them — not even a timestamp to hash on.

The server does mint an identifier: the `WebhookCall` row created at `:27-40`. It is simply never sent.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Point a webhook at an endpoint that returns 500 on first call and 200 afterwards.
2. Trigger any event.
3. Compare the two received bodies.

### Expected Behavior

Both attempts carry the same delivery id, so the consumer can treat the second as a duplicate.

### Current Behavior

Nothing is shared between the two bodies. `createdAt` differs. A consumer that acts on each delivery — issuing an invoice, filing a document — has no way to avoid doing it twice.

### Version

`main` @ 617f8cc (v2.16.0)

### Notes

Found during a code audit; verified by reading the handler and the retry configuration on current `main`. Not reproduced against a live endpoint.

I recognise this is closer to an enhancement than a defect, and that #3132 recently corrected the retry documentation — the gap is precisely that the retries are now documented while no idempotency key accompanies the payload.

Suggested direction: generate a delivery id when the job payload is built (so it stays constant across attempts) and expose it both in the body and as a header.

### Issue Description

`signature-pad-dialog.tsx` keeps the drawing in local state that is never reset when the dialog closes, so what is displayed and what gets committed can diverge.

- `:41-42` — `const [signature, setSignature] = useState<string>(value ?? '')`, declared **outside** the `<Dialog>` and never re-synced to `value`
- `packages/ui/primitives/dialog.tsx` does not pass `forceMount`, and `@radix-ui/react-dialog` renders `<Presence present={forceMount || context.open}>` → the **content is unmounted** on close
- On reopen, `<SignaturePad value={value}>` (`:117`) remounts from the **parent's** value (`signature-pad.tsx:45-47` initialises from `value` and only calls `onChange` on interaction), while the local `signature` still holds the abandoned drawing
- The confirm button is `disabled={!signature}` → **enabled**, and its `onClick` (`:133-139`) commits `signature`, not what is on screen

To be precise about what is *not* the bug: **Cancel alone commits nothing** — `:127-131` is a bare `<DialogClose>`, and `onChange` only fires from the confirm button. The defect is the stale local state, which surfaces on the *next* interaction.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the signature pad, draw a signature, click **Cancel**.
2. Reopen the pad — the canvas shows the parent's value (the previous signature, or nothing).
3. Click the confirm button **without drawing again**.

### Expected Behavior

Confirming commits what is displayed. After Cancel, the abandoned drawing is gone.

### Current Behavior

The abandoned drawing is committed. In the variant where there was no previous signature, the confirm button is already enabled over a visually empty pad.

### Version

`main` @ 617f8cc (v2.16.0)

### Notes

Found during a code audit; the unmount-on-close behaviour was verified in the Radix source rather than assumed. Not reproduced in a browser.

On a signing product this means a signature the user believes they discarded can end up on the document, which is why I am filing it despite the narrow reproduction path.

Suggested direction: reset in the dialog's `onOpenChange` — `setSignature(value ?? '')` on close — or key the content so local state is rebuilt.

### Issue Description

**`apps/remix/app/components/general/template/template-page-view-documents-table.tsx:178` and `:196`**
```jsx
isValueValid={(value) => [...DocumentStatusEnum.COMPLETED].includes(value as unknown as string)}
isValueValid={(value) => [...DocumentSource.TEMPLATE].includes(value as unknown as string)}
```

`DocumentStatusEnum.COMPLETED` is the **string** `'COMPLETED'`, so `[...'COMPLETED']` spreads to `['C','O','M','P','L','E','T','E','D']`. `.includes('COMPLETED')` is therefore **always false**, for both selectors.

Consequences in `search-param-selector.tsx`:
- `:18-22` — `value` always falls back to `'all'`
- `:41` — `<Select defaultValue={value}>` is **uncontrolled**, so `defaultValue` is only read on first render

The data *is* filtered server-side, so the table and the menu disagree. Worse, the filter cannot be cleared: `@radix-ui/react-use-controllable-state@1.2.2` only fires `onChange` when the value actually changes —

```js
React.useEffect(() => {
  if (prevValueRef.current !== value) { onChangeRef.current?.(value); prevValueRef.current = value; }
}, [value, prevValueRef]);
```

Since the internal value is already `'all'`, picking "Any Status" emits nothing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a template's page (`/t/<team>/templates/<id>`).
2. Set Status = Completed. The URL gets `?status=COMPLETED` and the table filters correctly.
3. Reload the page (or open the shared link).

### Expected Behavior

The menu shows "Completed", and selecting "Any Status" clears the filter.

### Current Behavior

The menu shows **"Any Status"** while the table stays filtered, and clicking "Any Status" does nothing — the filter can no longer be removed from the UI.

### Version

`main` @ 617f8cc (v2.16.0)

### Notes

Found during a code audit; the non-firing `onValueChange` was verified by reading the Radix source rather than assumed. Not reproduced in a browser.

Suggested direction: use a real list — `Object.values(DocumentStatusEnum).includes(...)` and `Object.values(DocumentSource).includes(...)` — **and** make the `Select` controlled (`value=` instead of `defaultValue=`), otherwise the display/URL mismatch survives any remount.

- `includeSenderDetails = true` → `Acme (billing@acme.com) on behalf of "Acme" has invited you to sign this document` — the team name is repeated and the human sender disappears.
- `includeSenderDetails = false` → `John Doe (john@acme.com) has invited you…` — **the individual's name and email are disclosed to the external signer in exactly the configuration chosen to avoid that.**

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In team email preferences, turn **off** "Send on Behalf of Team" (or on — both branches are wrong).
2. Send a document created on a V1 envelope.
3. Open the signing link as the recipient and read the first line.

### Expected Behavior

What the setting's own preview promises: with the setting on, the individual sender named "on behalf of" the team; with it off, the team only.

### Current Behavior

The two branches are swapped. With the setting off, the collaborator's name and email are shown to an external signer.

### Version

`main` @ 617f8cc (v2.16.0)

### Notes

Found during a code audit; verified against the server helper and the settings preview on current `main`. Not reproduced in a browser.

The V1 view is not dead code: `sign.$token+/_index.tsx:358` routes `internalVersion === 2` to V2 and everything else to V1, and `internalVersion: 1` is still written by `document-router/create-document.ts:73`, `create-document-temporary.ts:65`, `embedding-router/create-embedding-document.ts:34` and `template-router/router.ts:302,380` — plus all legacy data. The V2 header does not carry this sentence, so the bug is confined to V1.

**Neighbouring, not duplicate:** #3055 (*"DocumentInviteEmailTemplate message section ignores includeSenderDetails"*) and PR #3061 cover the same setting on the **email** side (`packages/email/templates/document-invite.tsx`). This one is the signing page.

### Issue Description

`envelope-distribute-dialog.tsx:80-91` seeds react-hook-form with `defaultValues`, which RHF reads **only on first render**:

```js
const form = useForm({ defaultValues: { meta: {
  emailId: envelope.documentMeta?.emailId ?? null,
  subject: envelope.documentMeta?.subject ?? '',
  message: envelope.documentMeta?.message ?? '', ... } } });
```

The open-effect at 230-240 resynchronises **only** `distributionMethod`:
```js
useEffect(() => {
  if (isOpen && envelope.documentMeta) setValue('meta.distributionMethod', envelope.documentMeta.distributionMethod);
}, [isOpen]);
```

And the component stays mounted for the whole editor session — `envelope-editor-header.tsx:199-209` and `envelope-editor.tsx:349` render it with no `key` and no conditional unmount. So whatever the subject and message were when the editor first rendered is what the dialog carries forever.

**The stale values are not merely displayed — they are written back.** `onFormSubmit` (179-181) posts `meta` to `envelope.distribute`, and `distribute-envelope.ts:26-45` calls `updateDocumentMeta({ subject: meta.subject, message: meta.message, ... })`.

The correct pattern already exists three files away: `envelope-editor-settings-dialog.tsx:320-323` does `form.reset(createDefaultValues())` on `[open]`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a draft in the envelope editor.
2. Open **Settings**, change the email subject and message, save.
3. Click **Send Document**.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog shows the subject and message just saved, and sends with them.

### Current Behavior

The dialog shows the **old** subject and message, sends the invitation with them, **and overwrites the saved `documentMeta` with the stale values**. The email has already gone out by the time anyone notices.

### Version

`main` @ 617f8cc (v2.16.0)

### Notes

Found during a code audit; verified by reading the dialog, its mount site and the server-side write on current `main`. Not reproduced in a browser.

Suggested direction: `form.reset({...})` in the `[isOpen]` effect instead of the single `setValue`.
